Megan / Jonas —

Quick internal note and proposal to make procurement + security happy. Below are two viable packaging options; both preserve ClearMed’s preference for amortized accounting while keeping Redwood’s implementation economics transparent.

Option A — 12-month amortized credit (recommended)
- Redwood issues a monthly credit equal to the agreed onboarding amount divided by 12; appears as a line-item credit on invoices.
- Example: $120,000 onboarding => $10,000 credit per month for 12 months.
- Benefit: aligns with procurement and keeps month-1 cash impact lower.

Option B — One-time offset credit with staged evidence milestones
- Redwood invoices onboarding fee; Redwood issues a one-time credit upon evidence delivery milestones (e.g., SOC2 snapshot + audit-log sample + KMS handover).
- Benefit: simpler bookkeeping for Redwood; procurement can accept if milestones are clearly defined.

Evidence deliverables (what we'll provide)
- SOC2 Type II report (PDF, signed)
- Audit-log export sample: sanitized CSV with schema + 30 sample rows (no PII) and ingestion map (JSON schema included in attached timeline).
- KMS/HSM configuration notes: architecture diagram (PDF) + key custody model description.

Notes on HSM vs KMS: HSM-backed key custody is a distinct premium line item. The addendum can offer two SKUs: KMS-managed keys (default) and optional HSM custody (additional recurring fee). If ClearMed wants HSM included in the amortized credit, we’ll need to quantify the delta.

I updated the addendum to a V2 that includes the 12-month credit example and explicit evidence routing to SecurityOps (see attached). Dev — can you confirm the size of the sanitized audit sample and whether we can produce the CSV + schema by week 2 of implementation?

Naomi Feldman
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
